summary:
M2 (Executor) implementation design for C:\Users\kaank\Desktop\uninstall\purge. Read-only pass: nothing edited, no cargo run. Read ENGINE_PLAN §3.1-3.6, §5.10, §7 (all), §10.1-10.3, §11.1-11.3 and checked the survey against code.

SURVEY CORRECTIONS (verified in code)
- bins/purge-engine/Cargo.toml ALREADY depends on purge-exec unconditionally (survey said it does not). `rig-exec = []` is empty; exec/undo/journal parse into Command::* and return Exit::NotImplemented (cli.rs ~L526-558, args.rs L62-107, L463-485).
- The executor input already exists: `purge-engine scan -o plan.json` writes the sidecar `plan.scan.json` = purge_plan::emit::ScanDoc (`purge.scan/0`) with full Candidates (action, blockers, decision, children), `absorbed`, `policy_version`, `mode`, `plan_hash`. No new plan schema is needed; `exec --plan plan.json` reads the sidecar via cli/output.rs::sidecar_path and recomputes purge_plan::hash::plan_hash(items, policy_version, mode).
- plan_hash covers ALL top-level items (Blocked/Weak included) and has no notion of selection. The executor needs a selection rule (default: band Safe + preselected; rig-exec only: --select ids file) and must journal a selection hash.
- Candidate has NO scan-time FileId (only purge-source types.rs has file_id). §5.10 "FileId must equal the scan" cannot be met from the plan today. M2 design: VALIDATE pass at exec start captures FileId/volume serial/reparse tag/final path per item into the journal; the per-item re-check compares against that. True scan-time binding needs a Candidate field + scanner change = post-M1a integration (package M2-POSTM1A).
- purge-plan/src/order.rs stages are: registry values, registry keys, file system, then Task, FirewallRule, Service, Package. ENGINE_PLAN §7.1 puts tasks/firewall (3) BEFORE registry and service deletion (8) after files. Consistent for everything M1a can emit (registry, files, AppX last); diverges once M1b emits services/tasks. Executor does not re-sort (order is hash-bound) but verifies the invariant "nested child before parent" and refuses otherwise.
- Action enum = {Quarantine, DeleteKey, DeleteValue, EditSegment, RemoveDirIfEmpty, RemovePackage, ReportOnly}. There is no Action for services/tasks/firewall, default-value change or MRUList edit, and Action is matched exhaustively in purge-plan (decide/order/empty_after) and purge-policy (band/harm), so adding variants touches M1a crates. M2 keeps Action unchanged and introduces an executor-internal ExecOp resolved from (Target, Action).
- purge-win: no cfg(feature="write") item anywhere; no scm/taskschd/firewall/rm/sr/taskdialog modules exist at all (read or write). Already present and reusable: fs::FileHandle (open with OPEN_REPARSE_POINT, metadata incl. n_links, FileId{volume_serial,id}, final_path, reparse_tag), fs::volume_info/is_fixed, fs::long_path, reg::Key (raw type + raw bytes values, link_target/is_link, security with TI check), reg::current_control_set, sid::is_admin_only_writable(path) (path + every ancestor, reparse point => false; admin set includes TrustedInstaller). sid::file_sd_facts is private.
- purge-guard is pure (no I/O): deny::DenyList::check(&Target, &Exemptions) and canon::GuardEnv (has purge_dirs; rules fs.purge deny %ProgramData%\Purge and *:\.purge-q). Execute-time re-check = a new pure module fed with handle facts, plus deny::check on both the lexical and the final path. GuardEnv is built live in bins/purge-engine (main.rs settings + pipeline.rs).
- purge-model/lib.rs doc already says journal/inverse types arrive in M2; none exist. tools/xtask/src/check_deps.rs already enforces purge-mcp allowlist {purge-model, purge-rpc} and no purge-win/write.
- Rig: vm/rig.ps1 pushes target\release\purge-engine.exe or -Engine <file> (file must be named purge-engine.exe); rigtool commands snap/diff/truth/ambient/score/convert/baseline/invdiff; no exec phase, traps, deep snapshot or reboot path. install/ has only README.md.

KEY DESIGN DECISIONS
1. Input and binding: exec loads ScanDoc sidecar; refuses unless recomputed hash == doc.plan_hash == --confirm, plan.json items equal to_plan0 projection order, and every selected item passes resolve(Target, Action) -> ExecOp. Never executes Blocked, hard-blocked, ReportOnly, undecided, or RegValueChanged items. Reversibility::None (RemovePackage) needs an explicit irreversible acknowledgement (rig flag now, broker prompt in M3).
2. ExecOp (in purge-model exec types): QuarantineMove, RemoveDirIfEmpty, DeleteKeyTree, DeleteKeyIfEmpty, DeleteValue, EditSegment, RemovePackage, plus DeleteService/DeleteTask/DeleteFirewallRule (typed packages, deferrable). Inverse: MoveBack{quarantine_path, original_path, file_id, volume_serial}, RestoreKeyTree{backup, sha256}, RestoreValue{backup, sha256}, ReinsertSegment{index, segment, written_value_hash}, RecreateDir{attrs, sddl}, RecreateKey{backup}, RecreateService/Task/FirewallRule{definition file, sha256}, None.
3. On-disk layout: C:\ProgramData\Purge\sessions\<session>\{journal.jsonl, plan.scan.json, report.json, reg\<op>.regbackup.json, def\<op>.json}; sessions\index.json (Users: read); Quarantine\<session>\<op>\<leaf>; X:\.purge-q\<session>\<op>\<leaf> on other fixed NTFS/ReFS volumes. Session id = UTC timestamp + 64 random bits.
4. Journal (purge.journal/1, JSONL): header{session, plan_hash, selection_hash, policy, mode, engine version, volumes} ; validated{item, facts}; intent{op_id, item, exec_op, inverse, backup path + sha256, pre-facts}; done{op_id, outcome: done|vanished|skipped(reason)|held_retry|pending_reboot|failed(code)}; group boundary every <=64 intents with FlushFileBuffers; commit | aborted; later undo_intent/undo_done/undo_conflict, reconcile, expire records. Reader tolerates one torn trailing line only.
5. Per-item sequence: live gate (G1 handle facts, G2 on lexical+final, G3, G6, G7, G10, G11, G13, ChangedSinceScan => skip) -> backup written, flushed, read back, hashed -> intent flushed -> act on the SAME handle the gate inspected -> verify -> done. Batch never aborts except on backup/journal write failure. Purge never raises its own access (no take-ownership/ACL edits/SeBackup for deletes); access denied => failed(AccessDenied) reported.
6. Storage roots are a library parameter (StorageRoots), never an env var; a relaxed-integrity constructor exists only under cfg(test)/feature test-support so unit tests run unelevated in temp dirs. Fault injection (PURGE_FAULT_AT=<point>[:n] => abort) only under purge-exec feature fault-inject, enabled by purge-engine's rig-exec.
7. M1a isolation: M2 packages touch purge-model (new files + one mod line), purge-win (new files), purge-guard (new file), purge-exec, bins/purge-engine (new cli/exec file + small edits to cli.rs/args.rs in one late package), tools/xtask, install/, vm/. They only READ purge-plan (hash, emit::ScanDoc, collapse::nests_in). Everything needing purge-scan/purge-plan/purge-policy edits is collected in M2-POSTM1A.

Model routing per user memory: critical -> Fable medium; high -> Opus high; medium -> Opus medium; trivial -> Sonnet. 26 packages in 9 waves.

packages.title: Scaffolding: manifests, module lists, stub files
packages.scope: Only manifests and module lists, so later waves never share a file. (a) Workspace Cargo.toml: add base64 (for name_b64) to workspace deps if not hand-rolled. (b) purge-exec/Cargo.toml: add sha2, base64, features `fault-inject` and `test-support`; lib.rs declares modules storage, journal, fault, regbackup, regfile, gate, act_fs, act_reg, act_typed, locked, prepare, plan_in, execute, undo, recover, expiry, report, with one empty stub file each (doc comment only). (c) purge-win/Cargo.toml: add windows-sys features Win32_System_Restore, Win32_System_RestartManager, Win32_System_Services, Win32_System_WindowsProgramming as needed; lib.rs declares `#[cfg(feature="write")] pub mod fs_write; reg_write; sr; rm; scm; taskschd; firewall; appx_write; pub mod secure;` (secure is read-side SD facts) with stub files. (d) purge-model/lib.rs: one line `pub mod exec;`; exec.rs declares `pub mod journal; pub mod regbackup; pub mod session; pub mod op;` with stubs. (e) purge-guard/lib.rs: `pub mod live;` + stub. (f) purge-engine/Cargo.toml: `rig-exec = ["purge-exec/fault-inject"]`. (g) rigtool main.rs: mod lines + dispatch arms for `deep`, `fidelity`, `execdiff` calling stub cmd fns. No behaviour.
packages.acceptance: cargo build --workspace, cargo build -p purge-win --features write, cargo build -p purge-engine --features rig-exec and cargo build in vm/rigtool all succeed; xtask check-deps still passes; existing tests unchanged and green; no file of purge-scan/plan/harvest/identity/policy touched.
packages.tests: Build-only plus existing suite (use a private CARGO_TARGET_DIR). No new tests.

packages.title: purge-model exec types: ExecOp, Inverse, journal records, regbackup/1, session index
packages.scope: Pure serde + JsonSchema types, schema-id newtypes like PlanSchema. op.rs: ExecOp (QuarantineMove, RemoveDirIfEmpty, DeleteKeyTree, DeleteKeyIfEmpty, DeleteValue, EditSegment, RemovePackage, DeleteService, DeleteTask, DeleteFirewallRule), `resolve(&Target, Action) -> Result<ExecOp, Mismatch>` (the only legal pairs; RegValueChanged and ReportOnly never resolve), Inverse (MoveBack, RestoreKeyTree, RestoreValue, ReinsertSegment, RecreateDir, RecreateKey, RecreateService, RecreateTask, RecreateFirewallRule, None), ItemOutcome (Done, Vanished, Skipped{reason}, HeldRetry, PendingReboot, Failed{code}), SkipReason incl. ChangedSinceScan, NoLongerEmpty, GateBlocked{blocker}, NoVerifiedBackup, CapExceeded. journal.rs: `purge.journal/1` Record enum (Header, Validated, Intent, Done, GroupEnd, Commit, Aborted, UndoIntent, UndoDone, UndoConflict, Reconcile, Expire) with FileFacts {final_path, file_id hex, volume_serial, reparse_tag, attributes, n_links, is_dir, size} and RegFacts {subkeys, values, is_link, owner}; backup refs carry path + sha256. regbackup.rs: `purge.regbackup/1` (KeyNode: name_b64, class, sddl owner/group/dacl, last_write_time, link flag, values[{name_b64, type u32, data_b64}], children) plus ValueBackup. session.rs: SessionIndex/SessionSummary for sessions\index.json (ids, app, times, counts per outcome, backup_bytes, expiry dates per class 30d/180d/1y, pending_reboot, state Open|Committed|Aborted|Undone|PartiallyUndone), ExecReport and UndoReport (CLI JSON output; rigtool reads these).
packages.acceptance: Every type round-trips fixed JSON samples byte-for-byte; unknown schema ids are rejected; resolve() table matches the summary and is total over Target x Action in a test; JSON Schemas generate; non-UTF-16-clean names and embedded NULs survive via base64.
packages.tests: Unit tests in each file (round-trip, schema-id rejection, resolve table exhaustive, base64 edge cases: empty name, lone surrogate, 16k-byte value).

packages.title: purge-win write: handle-based file ops, boot-time moves, SD facts
packages.scope: Thin, policy-free wrappers. fs_write.rs (cfg write): MoveHandle::open(path) = CreateFileW(DELETE|SYNCHRONIZE|FILE_READ_ATTRIBUTES, share R/W/D, OPEN_EXISTING, OPEN_REPARSE_POINT|BACKUP_SEMANTICS) exposing metadata/file_id/final_path/reparse_tag on that same handle; rename_into(&self, dest_dir_handle or absolute dest, replace=false) via SetFileInformationByHandle(FileRenameInfoEx) with fallback FileRenameInfo, never replacing; remove_dir_if_empty_by_handle (FileDispositionInfoEx on a handle opened with OPEN_REPARSE_POINT; maps DIR_NOT_EMPTY); delete_by_handle for files and for reparse points themselves (removes the link, never the target) used only by expiry; create_dir_secure(path, sddl) (CreateDirectoryW with SECURITY_ATTRIBUTES, fails if exists); set_attributes_by_handle (hidden|system|not-content-indexed); flush(handle); move_delay_until_reboot(src, dst) (MoveFileExW MOVEFILE_DELAY_UNTIL_REBOOT, no REPLACE_EXISTING); pending_renames() read of PendingFileRenameOperations(+2) as raw pairs and remove_pending_pairs(&[(src,dst)]) that rewrites only by removing exact own pairs under a compare-before-write check; list_streams(path) (FindFirstStreamW) for ADS. secure.rs (read): dir_security(handle) -> {owner_sid, group, dacl_protected, aces} via GetSecurityInfo on a handle, and sddl string of a handle. Typed error enum distinguishing NotFound, SharingViolation, AccessDenied, DirNotEmpty, NotSameDevice, Other(code). All paths go through fs::long_path (long paths, trailing dots/spaces preserved).
packages.acceptance: All functions are cfg(feature="write") except secure.rs; cargo tree for purge-mcp unchanged. A handle opened on a junction/symlink renames or deletes the link itself and leaves the target untouched. Rename never overwrites an existing destination. Cross-volume rename returns NotSameDevice. remove_pending_pairs leaves foreign pairs byte-identical.
packages.tests: Unit tests in temp dirs created by the test (unelevated): rename file/dir/junction (reuse the junction helper in fs.rs tests), >260-char path, trailing-dot name, read-only+hidden file, hard-linked file keeps link count, dir-not-empty mapping, secure-dir creation + SD readback, ADS listing. PendingFileRenameOperations logic tested on a pure function over value bytes (no HKLM writes in unit tests); the real registry write is VM-only.

packages.title: purge-win write: link-refusing registry write primitives
packages.scope: cfg(write). WKey::open(root, path, view, access) always with REG_OPTION_OPEN_LINK and explicit KEY_WOW64 view, exposing is_link, info (subkey/value counts, class, last write), raw values, security SDDL (owner/group/dacl), subkey names; delete_subkey(parent, name) = RegDeleteKeyExW(view) (single key, fails if it has subkeys); delete_value; set_value_raw(name, type u32, bytes); create_subkey(parent, name, class, sddl, volatile=false) failing if it exists (REG_CREATED_NEW_KEY required, never REG_OPTION_CREATE_LINK); set_security(sddl) only on keys Purge itself just created during undo; flush_key. No RegDeleteTree, no RegSaveKey, no privilege enabling. Root handles for HKLM and HKU only (no HKCR, no HKCU alias).
packages.acceptance: Opening a REG_LINK key returns the link key itself with is_link=true, never its target. delete_subkey on a key with children fails. create_subkey on an existing key fails. Exact raw bytes round-trip for REG_SZ without terminator, odd-length data, REG_NONE with data, type values above 11.
packages.tests: Unit tests under HKU\<current SID>\Software\PurgeTest-<random> created and removed by the test (unelevated), including a REG_LINK created by the test helper, both WOW64 views, class strings, and a restricted-DACL key.

packages.title: purge-win: restore point (srclient) and Restart Manager
packages.scope: sr.rs (write): create_restore_point(description) -> SrOutcome {Created{seq}, Throttled{seq}, Disabled, Failed(code)} via SRSetRestorePointW(BEGIN_SYSTEM_CHANGE, APPLICATION_UNINSTALL) + END; throttle detected by comparing the returned sequence number with the latest existing one (read side: latest_sequence()); never touches SystemRestorePointCreationFrequency. rm.rs (write): RmSession::start, register_files(&[paths]) (files only), lockers() -> Vec<{pid, start_time, app_name, service_name, type, restartable}>, end; no RmShutdown/RmRestart in M2 (closing apps needs consent = M3) - expose shutdown() but leave it uncalled by exec unless an explicit allow flag is passed.
packages.acceptance: Both modules compile only with write; RM lockers correctly reports a helper process holding a temp file; sr returns Disabled (not an error) when System Protection is off.
packages.tests: Unit: RM lockers against a child process spawned by the test holding a file in a temp dir. sr: pure test of throttle decision from (before_seq, returned_seq, status); real creation is VM-only.

packages.title: purge-win: SCM, Task Scheduler, firewall, AppX removal wrappers
packages.scope: DEFERRABLE (see open question 1). Read + write halves per object so a full definition can be captured before deletion and recreated: scm (QueryServiceConfigW/Config2 all info levels, security SDDL, status; stop with timeout; DeleteService; CreateServiceW + ChangeServiceConfig2W + SetServiceObjectSecurity), taskschd (GetTask XML, DeleteTask, RegisterTask(XML) via COM), firewall (get rule by InstanceID, delete by InstanceID only, recreate from stored instance; choose INetFwPolicy2 or MSFT_NetFirewallRule and document), appx_write (RemovePackageAsync for a full name, current user and all-users variants). Write halves cfg(write).
packages.acceptance: Definition captured -> delete -> recreate yields an identical definition (minus runtime state) for a test service/task/rule created by the test in the VM. Firewall deletes never match by display name.
packages.tests: Pure unit tests for definition (de)serialisation and field mapping. Object-creating tests are #[ignore] and run only in the VM gate (they need admin and change system state).

packages.title: purge-guard live gate: pure execute-time verdicts from handle facts
packages.scope: Pure, no I/O, no purge-win dependency; defines its own plain fact structs (the executor fills them). check_path(lexical, PathFacts{final_path, reparse_tag, attributes, file_id, volume_serial, n_links, is_dir, fs_name, drive_fixed, owner_is_ti, has_ti_ace, links_inside_plan}, expected: Option<Validated>, deny: &DenyList, exemptions) -> Result<(), Blocker>: G1 final path must equal the canonical lexical path (separator-aware, case-folded with prefix::fold, \\?\ stripped) else ReparseMismatch; any reparse tag on the item => ReparseMismatch unless the op is 'remove the link itself' in expiry; file id + volume serial must equal `expected` else ChangedSinceScan (soft: skip); G2 deny::check on BOTH lexical and final path as Target::Path; G3 TrustedInstallerOwned; G6 n_links>1 with a link outside the plan => HardLinkOutsidePlan; G7 placeholder attributes RECALL_ON_OPEN/RECALL_ON_DATA_ACCESS/OFFLINE or cloud reparse tags => SyncRoot; G10 not fixed or fs not NTFS/ReFS => CannotBackUp. check_key(canonical key, KeyFacts{is_link, owner_is_ti, subkeys, values}, op) : G11 RegLink for any link on the key or (via caller-supplied ancestor facts) any ancestor other than the two resolved aliases; deny::check + containers::check again; G13 emptiness for *IfEmpty. check_undo_destination(original target, facts of the destination parent chain) for §7.8 (G2/G11 on destination, parent must not have become a reparse point). admin_only_ancestors verdict wrapper for boot-time moves (input: bool per ancestor + reparse flag). quarantine_destination_ok(dest, purge roots, volume serials equal). Own-store exemption: a function that authorises ONLY paths strictly inside the session's own quarantine/session dirs for executor-internal handle ops; everything else in Purge's dirs stays denied.
packages.acceptance: Property: for every path form in the existing canon tests, a final path differing from the lexical one in any segment yields ReparseMismatch; a lexical path that is clean but whose final path is deny-listed is blocked with the deny rule id; ChangedSinceScan is soft, all others hard. No std::fs / purge-win use in the module.
packages.tests: Table + property tests in live/tests.rs: junction parent inside install dir (final path elsewhere), 8.3 alias, case differences, trailing dot, volume-GUID final path, hard link count cases, placeholder attribute fakes, REG_LINK on leaf and on ancestor, CurrentControlSet and _Classes aliases accepted, HKCR rejected, undo destination under Purge's own dirs rejected.

packages.title: install/install.ps1 v1 with protected DACLs and pre-created-dir handling
packages.scope: Elevated-only script. Copies purge-engine.exe (+ kb) into %ProgramFiles%\Purge with admin-only ACL. Creates C:\ProgramData\Purge\{sessions,Quarantine,fp,kb}: owner BUILTIN\Administrators, protected DACL (no inheritance) SYSTEM:F + Administrators:F, and Users:R only on sessions\index.json (created empty `{}` document) plus traverse-only as required to reach it (decide and document the minimal ACEs on ProgramData\Purge and sessions for a standard user to open index.json without listing). If ProgramData\Purge already exists and fails the integrity check (non-admin owner, unprotected DACL, is a reparse point, or contains reparse points at the top two levels): never adopt and never recurse into it; rename it aside to Purge.rejected-<utc> using a non-following rename, then create fresh. Idempotent on a good tree. -Uninstall switch removes only Program Files copy, never data. No downloads, no Defender/SR settings changes, no signing.
packages.acceptance: SDDL of each directory equals the documented constant; re-run is a no-op; a user-pre-created directory or planted junction is renamed aside and reported; a medium-IL user cannot create a file or junction anywhere inside and can read only sessions\index.json. The exact SDDL constants are shared verbatim with M2-X-STORE (single documented source in install/README.md).
packages.tests: install-selftest.ps1: parse check + pure functions (SDDL builder, integrity verdict over a fake ACL object) runnable on the host without elevation; the real install checks run in the VM gate (traps: pre-created dir, planted junction, medium-IL attacker via LaunchMedium).

packages.title: rigtool: deep snapshot and fidelity compare (§10.3)
packages.scope: `rigtool deep --scope scope.json -o deep.json`: for the listed roots/keys/objects only (scope = plan targets + their parents + trap manifest), record per file: content SHA-256, attributes, ADS names+sizes+hashes, hard link count, FileId + volume serial, reparse tag + link target text (never traversed), owner + SDDL; per key: SDDL, class, values (type + data hash), link flag; services/tasks/firewall: full definition minus runtime state (status, PID, last run, next run). `rigtool fidelity --before a.json --after b.json --journal journal.jsonl [--ambient ambient.json] -o fidelity.json`: applies §10.3 comparisons and exclusions (registry LastWriteTime, parent-dir LastWriteTime, 8.3 names, ambient set), requires FileId equality only for items the journal says were renamed, and reports pass/fail per action type (QuarantineMove file, QuarantineMove dir, RemoveDirIfEmpty, DeleteKeyTree, DeleteKeyIfEmpty, DeleteValue, EditSegment, + typed) with every differing field listed.
packages.acceptance: Identical snapshots => 100% for every type; each single-field mutation in a fixture (content byte, attribute bit, ADS removed, link count, SDDL ACE, value type, value data, key class) is detected and attributed to the right action type; excluded fields never fail.
packages.tests: cargo tests in vm/rigtool with JSON fixtures and temp-dir captures (ADS, hard link, junction created by the test).

packages.title: Guest trap builder and trap manifest
packages.scope: m2-traps.ps1 builds, inside a synthetic app root C:\Program Files\PurgeTrapApp and its HKLM/HKU keys, each §10.2 trap and writes the manifest of protected objects (what must be byte-identical after exec) and expected executor outcome per trap: junction/dir symlink/file symlink pointing at a canary tree; hard link to a canary file outside the plan; junction PARENT inside the install dir (plan item path traverses it); >260-char path; trailing-dot and trailing-space names; read-only + hidden + system files; REG_LINK key pointing at a canary key (leaf and mid-path); TrustedInstaller-owned folder and key; attribute-faked placeholders (RECALL/OFFLINE attributes, cloud reparse tag if creatable); user-pre-created C:\ProgramData\Purge and a planted junction inside Quarantine/sessions (built at medium IL through LaunchMedium); planted junction in a user-writable ancestor for the boot-time-move path; forged user-store fingerprint; swap-after-validate races (a helper that replaces a validated dir with a junction between two engine steps, driven by PURGE_FAULT_AT pause points); expiry-walk junction inside an expired quarantine item. m2-fixtures.ps1 builds the benign per-action-type fidelity fixtures (file with ADS + hard link inside plan, nested dirs, key tree with all value types/odd data/class/custom DACL, PATH segment, multi-sz, the BCU nested-delete sequence) and emits a hand-built purge.scan/0 + plan with a correct plan hash is NOT possible from PowerShell, so it emits a `select` ids file and target list for `purge-engine scan --path` or a rig-only `plan from-targets` helper (see M2-CLI).
packages.acceptance: Script parses, is idempotent on a fresh snapshot, and the manifest lists every canary with a content hash. Each trap has a stated expected outcome (blocker name or 'link removed, target intact').
packages.tests: Parse + dry-run mode (-WhatIf style plan dump) exercised by vm/guest/tests/rig-selftest.ps1 additions owned by M2-RIG-RUN; real creation only in the VM.

packages.title: purge-exec storage: layout, integrity checks, quarantine roots, size cap, index
packages.scope: StorageRoots {data_root, policy}. On EVERY use (open_session, quarantine_dir_for(volume), list, expiry): open each of data_root, sessions, Quarantine, the session dir and op dir with OPEN_REPARSE_POINT and require: not a reparse point, owner Administrators or SYSTEM, DACL protected and equal in effect to the install SDDL (no non-admin write/delete-child ACE); on failure refuse AND rename the directory aside (never recurse, never delete). X:\.purge-q on other fixed NTFS/ReFS volumes: created with create_dir_secure (fails if a user pre-created it => refuse that volume, items become CannotBackUp), same check on every use, hidden+system+not-indexed. Same-volume proof by volume serial of source handle vs quarantine dir handle. Session id generation (UTC + random). Op dirs created by Purge only (create-new semantics). Size cap min(10 GB, 5% of volume) computed from index + planned backup bytes: refuse a run that would exceed, never evict. sessions\index.json atomic rewrite (temp + rename within the checked dir) keeping Users:R. Test-only relaxed policy under cfg(test)/feature test-support (skips owner check, keeps reparse checks).
packages.acceptance: A junction planted at any level (data root, sessions, Quarantine, session, op) is detected before any write and the tree is renamed aside; a pre-created .purge-q is never adopted; cap refusal returns a typed error with numbers; index survives a crash between temp write and rename (old or new, never torn).
packages.tests: Temp-dir unit tests with planted junctions at each level, wrong-volume detection (mocked serials through a small facts trait), cap arithmetic, index atomicity (fault point between write and rename).

packages.title: purge-exec journal writer/reader, hashing, fault points
packages.scope: Append-only journal.jsonl: JournalWriter::create (create-new, in a storage-checked session dir), append(record), sync() = FlushFileBuffers; write-ahead contract enforced by API shape: `intent()` returns a token only after the record is durably flushed, `done(token, outcome)` consumes it; groups of <=64 intents closed by GroupEnd + sync; commit()/abort(reason). JournalReader: parse all records, tolerate exactly one torn final line, reject anything else malformed, expose state machine: per op {intent only | done(outcome)}, session state, pending boot moves, undo progress. sha256_file(path) streaming helper used for backups. fault.rs: `fault::point("name")` no-op unless feature fault-inject AND env PURGE_FAULT_AT=name[:nth] matches => std::process::abort(); optional PURGE_FAULT_PAUSE=name:ms for the swap-race traps; exported const list FAULT_POINTS = [journal.header, backup.written, backup.verified, intent.flushed, act.before, act.after, done.before, group.end, commit.before, regdelete.mid, regrestore.mid, undo.intent, undo.act.after, index.write, expiry.mid, bootmove.registered] that the rig enumerates via `purge-engine journal fault-points` (rig-exec).
packages.acceptance: No API path lets an action run before its intent is flushed (compile-time token). Reader reconstructs the exact state after truncation at every byte offset of a sample journal (never panics; either valid prefix state or a typed corruption error). Without fault-inject the fault module compiles to nothing.

packages.title: purge-exec regbackup/1: link-refusing walk, verified write, restore, .reg generator
packages.scope: capture_tree(root key handle) : own walk opening every subkey with REG_OPTION_OPEN_LINK; ANY link anywhere in the subtree aborts the capture with RegLink (the item is then skipped, nothing deleted); records raw type, raw bytes, name_b64, class, owner/group/DACL SDDL, LastWriteTime, link flag; bounded by blast-radius limit (>50 keys => TooLarge unless the plan item is an absorbing Safe parent with counted children - take limit as parameter). capture_value. write_verified(path): write, flush, close, reopen, read back, deserialize, structural-equality check, SHA-256 => BackupRef; no verified backup => caller must not delete. delete_tree(root, backup): deepest first, single-key RegDeleteKeyExW(view) per key, re-opening each key with OPEN_LINK and refusing if it became a link or gained subkeys/values not in the backup (=> stop, report ChangedSinceScan; already-deleted children are restored from the backup = per-subtree all-or-nothing). restore_tree(backup, verify sha first): all-or-nothing per subtree with rollback of keys created so far on failure; conflict rules: root key already exists => conflict if under Installer\*, Services or COM (CLSID/Interface/TypeLib/AppID) roots, otherwise merge only if existing key is empty, else conflict (skip + report). restore_value: restore if absent; present with same type+data => already restored; different => conflict. Segment helpers: remove_segment (one read-modify-write, records index, original value hash and written value hash; for ';' lists and REG_MULTI_SZ, preserves type and terminators) and reinsert_segment (only if absent and current value hash == written hash or segment merely missing; reinsert at recorded index clamped). regfile.rs: pure generator regbackup/1 -> .reg (UTF-16LE BOM, `Windows Registry Editor Version 5.00`, escaped key/value names, dword, hex(2)/(7)/(b)/hex(N), line wrapping) on request only.

gate_procedure:
Per-wave code gate (host, no VM): with a private target dir (CARGO_TARGET_DIR=...\target\m2-<pkg>) run cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy -p <crate> (purge-win also with --features write; purge-exec with --features fault-inject,test-support; purge-engine with and without --features rig-exec), cargo test for the touched crates, cargo xtask check-deps, cargo test in vm/rigtool, and vm/guest/tests/rig-selftest.ps1. Unit tests may be destructive only inside temp dirs and an HKU\<SID>\Software\PurgeTest-<random> subtree that the test itself creates and removes; nothing touches HKLM, ProgramData or PendingFileRenameOperations on the host. A critical package is reviewed by a second critical-tier pass before the next wave starts.

VM gate (M2-GATE). Build: cargo build --release -p purge-engine --features rig-exec into a separate target dir (target\rig-exec) and pass it with -Engine; rigtool release build. VMs: Inbound-Win11-Test (LTSC) for the full matrix; Purge-CleanPro once for traps + fidelity (TrustedInstaller/Defender/Pro specifics). Always restore from the powered-off snapshot. One-time: restore rig-base, run setup-m2.ps1 (enable System Restore on C:, test-only frequency override), power off, save child snapshot m2-base.

G0 install hardening (m2-install): (a) fresh install.ps1 -> SDDL of ProgramData\Purge, sessions, Quarantine, fp, kb, index.json and Program Files\Purge equal the documented constants; re-run is a no-op. (b) Medium-IL attacker (LaunchMedium) pre-creates C:\ProgramData\Purge, and separately plants a junction at Quarantine and at sessions\<x>; install.ps1 and then `exec` must rename aside and refuse/recreate; canary targets unchanged. (c) Medium-IL user cannot create a file or junction inside, can read only sessions\index.json. (d) Pre-created D:\.purge-q (second volume if present) is never adopted.

G1 traps, 0 escapes (m2-traps): restore m2-base -> install.ps1 -> m2-traps.ps1 (builds traps + manifest with canary hashes) -> plan (scan --path / plan from-targets) with a selection that deliberately includes every trap item -> rigtool snap A + deep A -> exec --plan --confirm <hash> --select -> snap B -> rigtool execdiff (journal, report, traps manifest, ambient) -> expect guard_escapes = 0, collateral = 0, and each trap's outcome equal to the manifest's expected blocker (ReparseMismatch, RegLink, TrustedInstallerOwned, HardLinkOutsidePlan, SyncRoot, CannotBackUp, ChangedSinceScan for the swap-after-validate races driven by PURGE_FAULT_PAUSE). Also: exec with a wrong --confirm, a tampered sidecar and a reordered plan must refuse with zero filesystem/registry changes (snap A == snap B). Forged user-store fingerprint trap: scan must not produce executable items from it (plan-side check, recorded in the report). Scripted adversarial run: a medium-IL loop that keeps swapping dirs for junctions under a user-writable app root during exec; canaries must stay intact.

G2 round-trip fidelity, 100% per action type (m2-fidelity): restore -> install.ps1 -> m2-fixtures.ps1 -> deep A -> exec -> execdiff (collateral 0) -> undo --session -> deep C -> rigtool fidelity(A, C, journal). Required rows: QuarantineMove file (with ADS, read-only/hidden, long path, trailing dot), QuarantineMove directory tree, hard-linked file with all links inside the plan, RemoveDirIfEmpty, DeleteKeyTree (all value types, class, custom DACL, both views), DeleteKeyIfEmpty, DeleteValue, EditSegment (PATH ';' list and REG_MULTI_SZ), nested-delete sequence (child Safe + parent delete-if-empty; parent with an unowned child stays), plus Service/Task/Firewall if the typed packages are in scope; RemovePackage is recorded as Inverse None. Then two real apps end to end for realism (Notepad++ and 7-Zip or Git from apps.ps1): install, vendor uninstall, scan, exec preselected, execdiff, undo, fidelity. Partial undo (--items) on one run. Undo-conflict run: recreate a deleted value with different data before undo -> conflict reported, nothing overwritten. Backup tamper run: flip one byte in a regbackup file -> undo of that item refused, others restored.

G3 crash injection (m2-crash): enumerate `purge-engine journal fault-points`; for each point x {resume, rollback}: fresh fixture root (batched per boot), deep A, run exec with PURGE_FAULT_AT=<point> (process aborts), `journal recover` must list the session with a probe verdict, then resume -> end state equals an uninterrupted exec (execdiff clean) and a following undo gives fidelity 100%; or rollback -> deep equals A. Repeat the matrix for faults during undo. Three host hard power-offs (VBoxManage controlvm poweroff) at intent.flushed, regdelete.mid and commit.before, then boot, Wait-Agent, recover. Recover run twice must be idempotent. Journal truncated by the rig at a random byte -> recover handles a torn tail and refuses real corruption without acting.

G4 lock + reboot reconcile (m2-reboot): locker helper holds (i) a DLL under C:\Program Files\PurgeTrapApp (admin-only ancestors) and (ii) a file under a user-writable root. exec -> (i) PendingReboot with exactly our (src,dst) pair appended to PendingFileRenameOperations and all pre-existing pairs byte-identical; (ii) HeldRetry and NO PFRO entry (admin-only-ancestor rule). Guest reboot (Fast Startup already off) -> continuation job -> `journal recover`/reconcile: moved item FileId + volume serial match -> Done; undo restores; fidelity 100%. Mismatch scenario: before reboot the attacker replaces a user-influenced component so a different object lands in quarantine -> reconcile moves it back immediately and writes an alert. Undo before reboot removes only our pairs. Held item retried at the next run after the locker exits, through the handle-based gate.

G5 expiry walk (inside m2-traps): create a committed session, plant junction/dir symlink/file symlink at several depths inside its quarantine item (elevated planter, simulating a compromised store) and a top-level junction swap by a medium-IL user (must be impossible by DACL; verify), advance retention via a rig-exec-only clock override, `quarantine expiring` lists it, `quarantine purge --ids --yes-irreversible` -> links deleted, every canary target byte-identical, FileId-mismatch item refused. Size-cap refusal run with a tiny test cap.

G6 restore point: on m2-base, exec of a high-risk plan (forced mode or a service item) -> a restore point of type APPLICATION_UNINSTALL appears (Get-ComputerRestorePoint), second run within the throttle reports Throttled, and on rig-base (System Protection off) exec proceeds with a warning; SystemRestorePointCreationFrequency unchanged by Purge.

Exit: vm/truth/m2.sh aggregates into vm/results/m2-gate.{json,md}: guard_escapes 0, collateral 0, undo_fidelity 100% per row, crash matrix all pass, reconcile pass incl. mismatch, nested-delete pass, expiry never crosses a junction, install hardening pass. Any non-zero goes back to the owning package; the gate is re-run from the snapshot.
risks_and_questions: USER QUESTION 1 (scope): M1a/M1b produce no Service/Task/FirewallRule candidates yet and Action has no variant for them. Include service/task/firewall execute+undo in M2 now (packages M2-WIN-TYPED + M2-X-TYPED, tested with hand-built plans; about 2 L-size packages) or defer them to land with M1b's SYS-* scanners and gate M2 on files + registry + AppX(None) only? Recommendation: defer service/task/firewall, keep RemovePackage; M2 exit 'per action type' then means the types the engine can currently emit.

USER QUESTION 2: The plan hash covers all top-level items and there is no selection concept. Proposed: default selection = Safe + preselected; rig-exec `--select ids.json` may add Likely/Weak; journal stores a selection hash; M3's consent dialog shows plan hash + selection. Accept, or should `--confirm` bind the selection too (confirm = SHA-256(plan_hash || selection_hash))?

USER QUESTION 3: Scan-time FileId (§5.10) needs a new optional Candidate field filled by purge-scan (M1a crate) and possibly a planhash schema bump. Until M1a lands, M2 binds identity at exec start (validate pass) instead of at scan. OK as an interim, with the real binding in M2-POSTM1A? Should item fingerprints enter the plan hash?

USER QUESTION 4: ENGINE_PLAN §7.1 order (tasks/firewall before registry, service delete after files) differs from purge-plan/src/order.rs (API objects last: Task, FirewallRule, Service, Package). Fix order.rs after M1a, or amend §7.1? No effect on what M1a can emit today.

USER QUESTION 5: Closing apps / stopping services / restarting Explorer (§7.3, ladder step 3) needs consent, which is the M3 broker dialog. Proposed for M2: implement Restart Manager query only (report lockers), no shutdown unless an explicit rig flag; locked items go to boot-time move or held-retry. OK?

USER QUESTION 6: Where do the gates run? Proposed: full matrix on the LTSC VM with a new child snapshot m2-base (System Restore enabled, test-only frequency override set by the rig, never by Purge), plus traps + fidelity once on Purge-CleanPro. A second data volume in the VM is needed to test X:\.purge-q; add a small D: disk to the LTSC VM (new offline snapshot) or skip cross-volume in M2?

USER QUESTION 7: install.ps1 Users:R on sessions\index.json requires traverse (not list) ACEs for Users on ProgramData\Purge and sessions. Accept traverse-only ACEs on those two directories, or move index.json elsewhere? Also confirm signing stays out of M2 (open decision §11.3 item 4).

USER QUESTION 8: `plan from-targets` (rig-exec-only verb that builds a ScanDoc from a target list for synthetic trap/fidelity fixtures) is a test tool that fabricates Safe candidates; it never exists in release builds. Accept, or should fixtures only go through real scans (`scan --path`), which limits trap coverage for registry items?

Concurrency risk: bins/purge-engine (cli.rs, args.rs), purge-model, purge-guard, purge-win, vm/rig.ps1, vm/guest/riglib.ps1, rig-selftest.ps1 and RIG.md are all modified-but-uncommitted M1a files even though they are not on the 'being edited' list. M2 mostly adds new files there (one mod line per lib.rs in M2-S0), but M2-CLI and M2-RIG-RUN edit existing files; confirm no M1a fix agent is in them, and ideally get M1a committed before wave 0 so M2 work can be diffed and reverted cleanly. A separate git worktree is not usable while M1a is uncommitted (the worktree would lack it).

Build interference: several agents building the same workspace must each use a private CARGO_TARGET_DIR; M2-S0 changes Cargo.lock (new deps/features), which M1a agents will see on their next build. Do M2-S0 at a quiet moment and keep the dependency additions minimal (sha2 is already a workspace dep; base64 can be hand-rolled to avoid any new crate).

Trust of the on-disk ScanDoc: in rig-exec the plan comes from a file, so the executor must not rely on stored bands for safety. Mitigation in the design: executor re-runs deny + containers + live gates itself on every item and refuses Blocked/hard-blocked items, but it cannot re-run the evidence policy. The 'broker executes only plans it built from its own scans' rule (§3.1) is therefore only fully met in M3 (in-memory plan_id); state this in the review log.

Deny-list self-exemption: fs.purge rules deny %ProgramData%\Purge and *:\.purge-q. Executor-internal operations on its own quarantine must bypass deny only through the narrow own-store authorisation in purge-guard::live (strictly inside the current session's op dir, storage-integrity-checked); undo destinations get the normal deny check. A mistake here is the most likely source of an escape; M2-GUARD-LIVE and M2-X-STORE need the strictest review.

TOCTOU residue: FileRenameInfoEx by handle closes the source race, but the destination path and parent-chain checks are still path-based at some points (quarantine dir, undo destination). Mitigated by admin-only DACLs on quarantine and by re-checking the destination parent handle's final path; undo into a user-writable original location cannot be made race-free against a same-user attacker (consistent with the plan's honest trust statement). Hard-link G6 check on whole-directory moves is conservative and may over-block (files with n_links>1 whose other names are not in the plan), costing recall, not safety.

No-raise-access rule vs. traps: TrustedInstaller-owned or ACL-denied items will fail with AccessDenied or be blocked by G3; this is by design (no take-ownership, no SeBackup/SeRestore). Registry SDDL restore on undo sets security only on keys Purge itself recreates; restoring an owner other than the caller may need SeRestorePrivilege, which the plan forbids for deletes but does not address for undo. Proposed: restore DACL always, owner/group best-effort without enabling privileges, report a Partial fidelity note if the owner differs; this could fail 'key SDDL' in §10.3 for non-admin-owned keys. Needs a decision or a §10.3 clarification.

Restore-point test needs System Restore enabled and the creation-frequency override in the test snapshot; the rig sets that key, the product never does. System Restore inside a VirtualBox guest with small disks can be flaky (shadow storage); treat G6 as must-pass on LTSC only.

PendingFileRenameOperations edits are racy with other installers by nature; MoveFileExW appends atomically, but removing our own pairs is a read-modify-write of the value. Design uses compare-before-write and removes exact pairs only; a concurrent foreign append between read and write could be lost. Keep the window minimal and document; consider leaving stale pairs harmlessly (source no longer exists) instead of rewriting when another writer is detected.

Crash matrix cost: restoring a snapshot per fault point is too slow (16+ points x 2 modes x exec/undo). The procedure batches per boot with a fresh fixture root per iteration and only 3 hard power-offs; the in-process crash matrix in crates/purge-exec/tests/crash.rs is the primary proof, the VM matrix the confirmation.

Host/guest build mismatch (host 26300.9974 vs Clean-Pro 26340.9882) does not affect the executor path, but real-app end-to-end runs in G2 depend on M1a scan quality and baselines; use LTSC rig-base apps already scored in M1a so a fidelity failure is not confused with a scan problem.

Not covered by any M2 package (no producer today): default-value-change and MRUList-edit inverses of §7.8, SYS-DRIVER, boot-time delete (Reversibility None) beyond returning NeedsIrreversibleConsent, .reg export UI, history.* RPC methods (purge-rpc is M3). They are listed in M2-POSTM1A item 4 / left to M1b-M3.

cross_package_notes: M2-INSTALL: M2-MODEL / M2-X-STORE: index.json starts as the 2-byte document {}, so the SessionIndex reader must accept an empty object (serde defaults on every field).

M2-INSTALL: M2-X-STORE: create the temp file for the atomic rewrite of index.json with the Index descriptor at creation. Otherwise Users lose read access, because a new file in sessions inherits only the SYSTEM and Administrators ACEs. Session and op dirs, and X:\.purge-q, should use the Store constant. Its on-use check accepts a SYSTEM owner while install.ps1 does not; decide whether to align them.

M2-INSTALL: M2-RIG-RUN: Push-Tools copies only guest\*.ps1, so the rig must also copy install\install.ps1 into the guest. Run it elevated as `install.ps1 -Engine C:\cr\bin\purge-engine.exe -ReportPath <out>\install.json`; it picks up kb from <engine dir>\kb automatically. G0 should assert from report.json: renamed_aside entries, changed=false on a re-run, and `-Check` exiting 0.
M2-INSTALL: Possible later hardening, not in the spec: set the not-content-indexed attribute on ProgramData\Purge\Quarantine, as section 7.5 does for X:\.purge-q.

M2-INSTALL: VM gate G0 is still to run: a fresh install with the SDDL constants matched and a re-run that changes nothing; a medium-IL user who pre-creates the tree or plants a junction, which must be renamed aside with canaries intact; a medium-IL user unable to create files or junctions or list directories, but able to read sessions\index.json.

M2-RIG-TRAPS: M2-RIG-RUN (rig-selftest owner): add to vm/guest/tests/rig-selftest.ps1 a parse check of both scripts, plus `m2-traps.ps1 -DryRun -OutDir <tmp>` and `m2-fixtures.ps1 -DryRun -OutDir <tmp>` (exit 0, four files each). Also assert the trap dry-run manifest is JSON-equal to vm/truth/m2-traps.json. The dry run compiles the C# helper, so this also catches compile errors.

M2-RIG-TRAPS: M2-RIG-RUN exec-run order: `m2-traps.ps1 -Stage pre-install` -> install\install.ps1 -> `m2-traps.ps1` (post-install) -> `m2-fixtures.ps1`. Then plan from-targets for group 'main' from m2-traps-targets.json + m2-fixtures-targets.json, and exec. Then `m2-traps.ps1 -Action check -Label after-exec` and `m2-fixtures.ps1 -Action check -Phase after-exec`. Then undo, then `-Action check -Label after-undo` and `m2-fixtures.ps1 -Action check -Phase after-undo` (that last one also compares every fidelity field). Groups race-a and race-b each need their own exec, with helper.env (PURGE_FAULT_PAUSE=name:ms) and `m2-traps.ps1 -Action swap -TrapId <id>` started in the background first. Group 'locked' belongs to m2-reboot, with `-Action plant-boot-junction` after the reboot. The expiry trap needs `-Action plant-expiry-junction` before `quarantine purge`. Default output dirs are C:\cr\out\m2-traps and C:\cr\out\m2-fixtures; pass -OutDir to put them in the run dir.

M2-RIG-TRAPS: M2-CLI: `plan from-targets` should read purge.rig.targets/0: {schema, source, origin:'ManualUser', targets:[{id, trap, group, target:<purge-model Target JSON>, action:<purge-model Action name: Quarantine|DeleteKey|DeleteValue|EditSegment|RemoveDirIfEmpty>}]}. The consumer filters by group. Paths may end in '.' or ' ' or exceed 260 characters on purpose.

M2-RIG-TRAPS: M2-X-JOURNAL / M2-X-EXEC contract assumptions:
- PURGE_FAULT_PAUSE uses the format name:ms. The race traps use intent.flushed:8000 and act.before:8000.
- The swap helper triggers on any journal.jsonl line that contains the JSON-escaped item path and the substring "intent" (case-insensitive). If the journal's record encoding differs, adjust the trigger in m2-traps.ps1 (swap action).

M2-RIG-TRAPS: M2-INSTALL: the pd-plant-denied trap expects a medium-IL user to be unable to create files or junctions in C:\ProgramData\Purge, Quarantine or sessions, and unable to list Quarantine, but able to read sessions\index.json. The pd-precreated trap expects the user-created tree to be renamed to C:\ProgramData\Purge.rejected-* (post-check looks for purge-trap-precreated.txt inside it).

M2-RIG-TRAPS: First VM run: verify the registry half of the native helper on a fresh LTSC snapshot: REG_LINK create/NtDeleteKey, the SetKeySddl two-step fallback for TrustedInstaller-owned keys, and reglink-user (marked optional). Then run build twice to confirm idempotency and run `-Action reset` once.
